environment: Disposable local Linux ARM64 VM, 1 CPU and 2 GiB RAM
observed: The extracted cp-materialize function, using actual native FS2 against the VM filesystem, restored a fresh destination, refused an existing stage created after the mocked existence check while preserving its sentinel, and refused a destination created after the check while retaining its partial tree. Replacing no-replace T with ordinary L or replacing exclusive I with an allow-existing mkdir made the fixture return failure.
limits: The Git, bundle and JSON helpers are stubs and the race is staged before execution by deliberately forcing the earlier existence check false. This is not an end-to-end checkpoint restore, concurrent adversarial test, Darwin runtime test or proof that the tree can be shared by writers. The destination parent still requires exclusive ownership.
